editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-learning city of about 1.1 million. Its retail is heavy on pharmacy & health retail and coaching & training, and thin on desserts, sweets & ice cream and cafés, tea & coffee — and 51% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 35% of Kolkata's. 5.65 chain outlets per lakh residents against 16.14 in Kolkata; 23 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 9, Bata 5, Domino's 4.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 3.4% (Kolkata 2.2%); education 13.8% (Kolkata 9.7%); offices 6.7% (Kolkata 11.0%); food & beverage 6.4% (Kolkata 9.0%). Raw counts would mislead because Kolkata is mapped more completely (66,688 places against 2,697), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 6 zones hold 51% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Burnpur alone has about 206,000 residents and 25 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is more concentrated than in Kolkata. 52% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Kolkata 46%). The largest cores are Sbgorai Road (452 places) and Court (303).

The widest brand gaps against Kolkata. Apollo Pharmacy 9 outlets vs 186; Café Coffee Day 3 outlets vs 88; MedPlus 0 outlets vs 78. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Kolkata, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Burnpur and Sbgorai Road are the largest zones by residents (206,000 and 133,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 52% of all commercial places, and Sbgorai Road alone lists 452.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Sbgorai Road holds 19 of the 65 tracked chain outlets, and Burnpur adds 14.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Court and Ushagram lead on education places (73 and 46, with 31 and 14 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Burnpur and Dakhin Dhadka. The blue cores include Sbgorai Road.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (66,688 places in Kolkata against 2,697 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Kolkata; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Kolkata, Asansol's mapped places over-index on automotive (3.4% vs 2.2%), education (13.8% vs 9.7%), shops & retail (16.8% vs 14.3%) and under-index on offices (6.7% vs 11.0%), food & beverage (6.4% vs 9.0%), services & crafts (6.2% vs 8.3%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 65 outlets of 23 tracked national brands within 8 km — 5.65 per lakh residents against Kolkata's 16.14 (1135 outlets of 40 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Kolkata are Apollo Pharmacy (9 vs 186); Café Coffee Day (3 vs 88); MedPlus (0 vs 78). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Kolkata's, so low means thin by Kolkata's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Asansol's age mix against Kolkata: children (0–14) 21.7% vs 18.6%, 15–24 19.6% vs 18.4%, working age 50.6% vs 52.7%, 60+ 8.1% vs 10.3%. Under-25s are 41% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 5.0% of mapped places against 6.0% in Kolkata — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 4 (Kolkata 80), KFC 3 (Kolkata 38), Wow! Momo 3 (Kolkata 79), Pizza Hut 2 (Kolkata 36). No mapped outlet in either city: Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 1.2% of mapped places against 2.7% in Kolkata — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 3 (Kolkata 88). No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Point, Third Wave Coffee.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.5% of mapped places against 1.2% in Kolkata — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 2 (Kolkata 53). No mapped outlet in either city: Havmor, Theobroma, Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 0.7% of mapped places against 1.1% in Kolkata — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: DMart 4 (Kolkata 14), Reliance Smart / Fresh 4 (Kolkata 15), Big Bazaar 2 (Kolkata 17), Spencer's 2 (Kolkata 32). No mapped outlet in either city: Easyday, Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.9% of mapped places against 1.4% in Kolkata — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 9 (Kolkata 186). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 6.2% of mapped places against 5.2% in Kolkata — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 5 (Kolkata 71), Reliance Trends 3 (Kolkata 33), Raymond 3 (Kolkata 38), Tanishq 3 (Kolkata 20).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.2% of mapped places against 8.3% in Kolkata, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.9% of mapped places against 3.2% in Kolkata — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 4.3% of mapped places against 5.0% in Kolkata — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
